verdict.rationale: Morph's own docs officially support building with existing SDKs. Any OpenAI SDK can point at its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, the Anthropic Messages API is served natively, and the docs have an 'sdk/components' section. A community user confirmed the OpenAI-compatible endpoint works with an existing client tool. However, no Morph-published SDK package is evidenced, so this rests on third-party SDK compatibility. Missing for 10: a first-party Morph SDK package (e.g. npm/pip) with language coverage, an OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), SDK reference docs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Point any OpenAI SDK at https://api.morphllm.com/v1. One API key covers the open-weight chat models and the specialized tools
existing OpenAI code only needs a new `model` string
Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API, which Morph serves natively at `/v1/messages`.
This uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so got this working with my llm.datasette.io CLI tool
